prompt: Daniel wants to back up the current leases the DHCP server has assigned, ensuring that if the server needs a restart, he can restore the active leases. However, he's concerned about the size of this backup. Why might the dhcpd.leases file be larger than Daniel expects?
choices: Because it stores all the historic lease data
Because it includes the full DHCP server configuration
Because it caches DNS records for every client
Because it logs every DHCP packet received
explanation: The dhcpd.leases file is append-only, accumulating historic lease entries until it is periodically rewritten, which can make it larger than expected.
